cohort: 190 singleton pregnant women who gave birth to an appropriately grown infant at 28+0 to 33+6 weeks of gestation between 2011 and 2014
finding: In appropriately grown infants who were born at 28+0 to 33+6 weeks of gestation, cesarean delivery did not improve neonatal outcomes compared to vaginal delivery, but increased the risk of 5-minute Apgar score <7.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery did not improve neonatal outcomes compared to vaginal delivery, but increased the risk of 5-minute Apgar score <7.
